clue.text: Close entertaining lawsuit wrapped up

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests holds them within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the close of something is its end
a lawsuit is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A court case is wrapped up with entertainment along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrapped up has been enclosed in a covering, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Feature of laciest pants?

indicators.note: pants as slang for rubbish or badly done, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wondering what makes the frilliest knickers special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' reads as underwear but is the British slang for poor, signalling an anagram. The waistband of pants is the feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretchy waistband material is a standard feature of underpants, lacy ones included.

clue.text: Expenses of Greek island trips on vacation

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

indicators.note: a word on vacation has emptied out its middle, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: The bills run up on holiday trips to a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges or outlays one must pay are the expenses of an activity.

clue.text: Lacking wings, asked all vets for any small bones

indicators.note: each word loses its wings, the letters at either end

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone asking every vet whether there are any small bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete frameworks of bones are what the word names, so 'bones' stands for them loosely.

clue.text: Training medic badly

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
ill can mean badly, as in 'ill-advised'

explanation.surface: A doctor doing his training poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetitive practice exercises, as on a parade ground, are a form of training.

clue.text: Commanded European to wear gold, diamonds and crimson?

indicators.note: the European letter is dressed in the jewels and colour, so it sits inside them

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe is ordered to put on gold, diamonds and red finery.
explanation.definitionFit: To have commanded someone is to have given them instructions, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Arranged grandiose changes

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Grand plans are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged has been put in order or planned, a synonym.

clue.text: Society girls getting to grips with tango? They're liabilities!

indicators.note: gripping something holds it inside the hands, so one piece sits within

parts.note: debs are debutantes, young women entering high society
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Debutantes learning to tango are a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is a liability on a balance sheet, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Shape reportedly ruined view

indicators.note: a report is heard, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: ruined means wrecked and a view is an angle, a point of view

explanation.surface: News that a fine view has been spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with right angles is a basic geometric shape.

clue.text: Ultimately uncontrolled rage over son's threats

indicators.note: in a down entry the earlier pieces sit over the last one
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: rage is extreme anger
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Uncontrolled fury over a son's menacing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Perils or hazards are threats, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Replying to a call containing bad news

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the next one within them

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: bad news here is news made bad, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Picking up the phone only to hear bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replying to a call' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Replying'; 'a call' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Replying to a call is responding to it, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Outlaw eating commanding officer's food

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
CO is the military abbreviation for commanding officer; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A bandit tucks into an officer's rations.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork is a common breakfast food, so this is an example of the broad category.

clue.text: Experience defeat, as team hides

indicators.note: the words that follow conceal the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A sports team goes into hiding after suffering a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a taste of something is to experience it briefly, as in tasting defeat.

clue.text: Garden with lights on head?

parts.note: a bird that lights on a branch settles or lands there
a head or headland is a cape jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A garden with lamps fixed to someone's head, an odd image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garden' is a verb here: to lay out and plant grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To garden an estate is to shape its grounds with plants and features, the verb sense.

clue.text: Company with million quid making chemicals

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling, so many quid are pounds

explanation.surface: A firm earning a million pounds by manufacturing chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical substances made of bonded elements are known by this name in chemistry.

clue.text: Worried actor taken in by fashion for fleet of cars

indicators.note: the rearranged word is taken inside the fashion word

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about into a new order

explanation.surface: An anxious actor fooled by a fashion for luxury cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession of official vehicles is a fleet of cars moving together.

clue.text: Mischievously and proudly dropping husband after first bit of nookie

indicators.note: the trimmed word is placed after the letter from nookie
the first bit of a word is its opening letter
the husband letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: acting proudly is acting haughtily

explanation.surface: A cheeky, proud spouse behaving badly after a bit of fun in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving mischievously is behaving badly in a playful way, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Cold periods in prisons

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ages are long periods of time

explanation.surface: Spells of cold weather inside jails.
explanation.definitionFit: Barred enclosures that confine animals or people serve as prisons.

clue.text: Put right, I might stand thus?

definitions.meaning: a mistake put right has been fixed
the idiom 'I stand ..., ' said on admitting a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone owns up after being set straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed errors are put right, and the phrase 'I stand ...' admits being wrong.

clue.text: Pens, we're told, ceremonial forms

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: to pen a letter is to write it, so he pens means he writes

explanation.surface: A list of pens and printed ceremonial forms, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious rituals are formal ceremonies, the set forms of worship.

clue.text: Cleric with kinship to regularly call again

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric's title

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the words before

explanation.surface: A vicar with family ties drops in once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to visit, so calling again is a return visit.

clue.text: What superhero might have on the outside?

definitions.text: What superhero might have on the outside?

parts.words: What superhero might have on the outside?
parts.note: comic-book heroes such as Superman famously wear their pants over their tights

explanation.surface: A question about a superhero's costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments normally hidden beneath clothes are worn externally by caped heroes like Superman.

clue.text: Journalist supporting race broadcast

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: a relay is a team race
ED, an editor, is the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter backing a race that is being televised.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on a signal or message is to broadcast it, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Puts on coat perhaps and disappears crossing river

indicators.note: the word for disappearing spans the river, holding it within

parts.note: something that disappears vanishes
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone throws on a coat and vanishes across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' is a coat of paint or lacquer, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying a glossy protective finish to wood is putting a coat of lacquer on it.

clue.text: Home help upset country

parts.note: being at home is being in

indicators.note: in a down entry an upset word is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper upset about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A South Asian nation is one example of a country.

clue.text: Shoot southern puritan

parts.note: a prig is a smugly moralistic person, a puritan

explanation.surface: An order to fire at a strait-laced Southerner.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stem with leaves is a young shoot of a plant.

clue.text: Carefully move front of loose supporting framework

parts.note: to ease something into place is to move it carefully

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Gently shifting a loose piece of scaffolding.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holding a canvas is a supporting frame.

clue.text: Blade, black, changing hands

indicators.note: left becomes right: one hand's letter is swapped for the other's

parts.note: sable is the heraldic term for black

explanation.surface: A black-handled knife passing from one owner to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved cavalry sword is a type of blade.

clue.text: Tolerate some of India's tandooris

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Putting up with only a portion of India's clay-oven dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with or bear something is a common sense, as in 'I can't bear it'.

clue.text: Refurbished library accepts computers etc with bad temper

indicators.note: the rearranged word takes in the next piece, holding it inside
a refurbished room is done up anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

explanation.surface: A grumpy reaction to the library's refit taking in new computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting crossly and peevishly is behaving with a bad temper, an adverb of manner.

clue.text: Some admitting blame for treatment

indicators.note: the outer word lets the next piece in, so it sits inside

parts.note: some people, as in 'some say', are referred to as they
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Some patients admit fault as part of their treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing care for body or mind is a course of treatment, a synonym.

clue.text: Setter maybe returning with post is a stroke of luck

indicators.note: returning means the dog word comes back, read from the other end

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, hence 'maybe'
to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler coming back with mail brings good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts as the crossword compiler; it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected blessing that arrives just when needed is a fortunate stroke of luck.
